elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New § 11.2A: "Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One". Corio is our party (the customer/ASP licensee); the element is disjunctive and this Agreement has no Order Form structure (fees sit in Exhibit B), so coverage of the Agreement itself suffices. Note the deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returned false only because the drafter used the proper name "Corio" rather than an alias token "Customer" - a deliberate choice, since § 1.6 defines "CUSTOMER(S)" as Corio's sublicensees; on substance the right runs to our party.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: § 11.2A: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One" - exactly 30 days, written, and unconditional (no cause, consent, or milestone trigger).

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: § 11.2A: "Commerce One shall refund to Corio, on a pro-rata basis, any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination." The words "on a pro-rata basis" are express, so this is not an inferred pro-ration from a post-termination period alone.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Already met and retained: § 11.2 limits Commerce One's termination to uncured material breach (30-day cure) and insolvency/assignment for creditors; no no-cause exit appears in §§ 11.1-11.3. § 11.1's 30-day notice runs only "prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal", i.e. natural-term non-renewal, which is assessed under RENEWAL and is not a mid-term convenience right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: § 11.2A gives 30 days' notice, which is outside the literal 60-90 day band (and better for us). This is why the fallback checklist is not complete; the preferred level is.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither §§ 11.1-11.3 nor Exhibit B's payment terms impose any early-termination fee, acceleration, or contingent instalment on Corio's exit, and the redline adds none, so no fee can exceed a three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Commerce One has no convenience right at all under retained § 11.2 (breach and insolvency only), which is stricter than the fallback.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply because Commerce One holds no convenience termination right; the only Commerce One notice mechanic is the § 11.1 non-renewal notice tied to term expiry, which is a RENEWAL issue.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met by the single inserted § 11.2A plus the already-compliant retained § 11.2. No element is merely promised in the margin comment.

The deterministic 'Customer convenience termination present: false' signal is a false negative from alias matching. The operative sentence grants the right to "Corio", our client, and the drafter correctly avoided the defined term "CUSTOMER(S)" (§ 1.6 = Corio's sublicensees), which would have granted the exit to third parties. Substantively the element holds.

Minimal: a missing-clause insertion of one sentence, no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no added procedures, and no "in whole or in part" surplus (correct, since there is no Order Form or partial-termination structure here). §§ 11.1-11.3 are retained verbatim, including the Customer-favourable mutual breach and insolvency rights, and no word outside the checklist is deleted or paraphrased.

Preserves intent: the refund obligation is confined to prepaid fees for the post-termination period, so it does not disturb Exhibit B's payment mechanics, the § 11.1 renewal cycle, or any survival/remedy allocation; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created, and no retained sentence contradicts § 11.2A.

Fallback is not independently complete only because of the 30-day notice (outside 60-90 days) - an over-achievement, not a defect. If Commerce One pushes back, the comment's offer to move to 60-90 days would still leave the fallback complete, since no early-termination fee exists and Commerce One has no convenience right.
No repair required. Optional polish only: if the parties later add Order Forms, extend § 11.2A to "this Agreement or any Order Form" so the right survives an order-based structure.
